header: "Dr." before a name, WHEN IT IS SHOWN (step 47a). The stored names have no title (checked on the live data: none of the main hospital's 63 executives starts with "Dr"), and I want them to stay that way: the name search (first word, surname, phonetic codes, "kumar as a middle word", alphabetical order) works on the plain name. So I add the title only at the moment of display, by the one rule below, in every place that builds or shows a person. Who gets "Dr.":

1. every person on the MEDICAL track of the designation table (Director(M&HS), Joint Director, Sr. Deputy Director, Asst. Director/Sr. Consultant, DMO/Consultant, ADMO/Specialist, Medical Officer): automatic, nothing to maintain;
2. the NON-MEDICAL employees (executives and non-executives) who hold a PhD and write "Dr." before their name: the data cannot tell, so I list their tickets in DR_TICKETS below.
This file has no server code, so the browser can use it.

symbols.name: DR_TICKETS
doc: Tickets of NON-MEDICAL employees who hold a PhD and write "Dr." before their name. One ticket per line, six digits, in quotes, a comma after each. Edit this list to add or remove one; the test (honorific.selftest.ts) checks the format and that no ticket is listed twice.

symbols.name: makeTitleFor
doc: The rule, for a given list of extra tickets (the tests use their own list).

symbols.name: makePhdHolder
doc: The small "PhD" badge on the card: I show it only for the people on the manual list (a non-medical employee with a PhD). A doctor has the title already and needs no badge.

symbols.name: isDoctorPerson
symbols.sig: const isDoctorPerson = (track: unknown, doctorOverride: unknown): boolean =>
doc: Is this person a doctor? Yes if on the medical track of the designation table, or flagged in the roster (doctor_override) because the designation is a managerial one although the person is a doctor.

symbols.name: withTitle
symbols.sig: export function withTitle(name: unknown, title?: string | null): string
doc: The name as shown: "Dr. ARIJIT CHAKRABORTY". A name that already starts with Dr / Doctor is left as it is, so it is never "Dr. Dr.".

symbols.name: stripDoctorTitle
doc: "Dr. Anil Kumar" typed into a search means the stored name "Anil Kumar": I treat a LEADING Dr / Dr. / Doctor as a title, not a word of any stored name. Anything else is returned as it is.

symbols.name: withTitlesInRows
symbols.sig: export function withTitlesInRows<T extends Record<string, unknown>>(rows: T[], people: ReadonlyArray<unknown> | null | undefined): T[]
doc: The rows of a table or CSV: the name column of a person with a title gets it too (found by the ticket), so the table says what the card says.
